# monthly macro monitor


key trends for the agency mbs investor
OCTOBER 2026


- **Market Backdrop:** Concerns about AI-related business models, funding, and valuations drove a flight to quality and increased demand for U.S. Treasuries and other high-quality investment alternatives in October. Interest rates retraced a significant portion of September’s sharp bond market selloff, with the 10-year Treasury yield ending the month back below 5%. The Bloomberg U.S. Treasury Index and the Bloomberg U.S. Agency MBS Index posted one-month total returns of 2.4% and 3.1%, respectively, each index’s best monthly performance since December 2023.
- **Employment:** Key employment measures released in October were weaker than expected. September U.S. nonfarm payrolls (NFP) increased by 29,000, well below the median estimate of 90,000, and July and August totals were revised down by 60,000 in aggregate. The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, above the median estimate. Despite these weaker-than-anticipated releases, employment trends are generally stable and point to a labor market that is cooling but not deteriorating.
- **Inflation:** Key inflation measures released in October moved higher on a year-over-year rate basis. Specifically, core CPI increased to 2.6% from 2.4%, above the median estimate of 2.5%, and core PCE increased to 3.1% from 3.0%, in line with estimates. Persistent inflation continues to be a key focus for the Fed and other policymakers, financial market participants, and American households, which, as Chairman Warsh emphasized during his October press conference, “are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the \[FOMC’s\] objective for close to six years.”
- **Federal Reserve and Monetary Policy:** The FOMC maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75-4.00% at its October meeting, in line with market expectations, following the 25 basis point rate hike in September. The 10-2 decision drew two dissents, both in favor of another 25 basis point increase. Chairman Warsh also announced that, while the FOMC will continue to meet eight times per year, one of its meetings in 2027 and two of its meetings in 2028 are expected to focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated, noting that “it’s equally important we reserve time and space, as an intellectually diverse group, for strategic deliberations.” Fed funds futures are currently indicating an approximately 75% probability of a rate hike in December. Read our[October Fed Report](https://agnc.com/the-fed-report-october-2026/) for more details.
- **Interest Rates and Agency MBS Spreads:** U.S. Treasury yields declined across the curve, with the 10-year yield falling 36 basis points, its largest monthly decline since July 2024, following its 54 basis point increase in September. Interest rate volatility eased modestly but remained elevated. Agency MBS spread volatility declined meaningfully from September levels, and spreads to benchmark rates were essentially unchanged month-over-month.
